title: A smooth separated curve is proper or affine
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be a smooth separated connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves]. Then $C$ is either proper over $k$ or affine over $k$.

source.place: Lemma 0A28 (varieties-lemma-dim-1-nonproper-affine: dim <= 1 separated finite type, no proper 1-dimensional irreducible component, then affine); a smooth connected curve is irreducible

proof.text: By [lem-sc-compactification], there are a proper smooth connected curve $\overline C$ over $k$ and an open immersion $j:C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ whose complement $S=\overline C\setminus C$ is a finite set of closed points. The hypothesis that $k$ is algebraically closed is part of [def-sc-curves], which is the curve notion used in the statement.

If $S$ is empty, the open immersion $j$ has all of $\overline C$ as its image and is therefore an isomorphism, so $C$ is proper over $k$ because $\overline C$ is proper. If $S$ is nonempty, the existing affine-open lemma [lem-sc-affine-open-proper] applies to $j$ and gives that $C$ is affine. These two cases exhaust the possibilities.
